about.title: Pacific Grove Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Pacific Grove's tree-lined streets and coastal drives see steady local and visitor traffic, and Monterey County records show 34 injury collisions here in the most recent final year, with 38 people hurt. Forest Avenue, Ocean View Boulevard, Sunset Drive, and Lighthouse Avenue account for a large share of reported crashes, and Thursday afternoons between 1 and 3 p.m. tend to see more reports than other times. Whether you were rear-ended near a shopping corridor or sideswiped along the coastal route, sorting out medical bills, lost income, and an insurance adjuster's calls can feel overwhelming while you're still trying to heal. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect Pacific Grove residents and visitors with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened and explain your options. There's no cost to talk, and attorneys in our network only get paid if your case results in a recovery. Getting informed early, before evidence fades or memories blur, often matters most.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash to file a personal injury claim, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city road crew — was involved. An attorney can flag deadlines early so you don't lose the chance to recover anything.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Both Ways
items.desc: California lets you recover damages even if you were partly at fault, with your share reducing the total rather than blocking your claim entirely. An attorney can help make sure the insurer isn't unfairly shifting blame onto you to lower what they owe.

items.title: No Cap Doesn't Mean No Fight
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, but insurers still push back hard on these amounts. Skipping a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer and letting an attorney handle communications can protect the value of your claim.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use these statements to find ways to reduce or deny a claim, even when the questions sound routine. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened on Forest Avenue or Sunset Drive during a busy afternoon?
items.answer: Crashes on higher-traffic Pacific Grove corridors like Forest Avenue and Sunset Drive, especially during Thursday afternoon peaks, often involve multiple witnesses and nearby businesses with camera footage. Preserving that evidence quickly matters, since footage can be overwritten and memories fade. An attorney connected through our service can help identify what evidence to secure early.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney, and there's no charge to have an initial conversation. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if your case results in a recovery.
